[P4] 出版者的话
古希腊圣哲亚里士多德曾说:“任何人都会生气,这没什么难的,但若要适时适所地以适当方式对适当对象恰如其分地生气,可就难上加难了。”我们现在讲的情绪管理指的就是要适时适所地对适当对象恰如其分地表达情绪。
现实生活中,人们越来越多地认识到情绪管理能力的重要性,因为这方面能力出众的人往往在各个领域都游刃有余;相反,此项能力差的人,虽然可能很聪明,但做起事来往往很吃力。
情绪管理能力虽部分得益于先天因素,但归根结底还得靠后天的学习和培养。幼儿时期是情绪管理能力培养的黄金时期。一个人在幼儿时期所获得的情绪经验和习惯会在大脑中形成永久的神经联结,对其身心发展影响很长远。
当前,亲子共读情绪管理类图画书这种情绪管理能力培养方式已被广泛认可。优质的图画书好比幸福的种子,通过父母的声音飞进孩子的耳朵里,植根在孩子的心底,施以阳光、雨露就能生根、发芽。
这套有趣的动物图画故事书温情脉脉,每一本都是有针对性地就孩子的某一种情绪话题展开,描绘孩子的心路历程,揭示其走出情绪困扰并解决问题的过程。每一本书都附有幼教专家精心撰写的导读,可作为家长亲子共读时的参考。
让我们在这套书的陪伴下,去享受一段美妙的亲子阅读之旅吧

[P5] 老师对你说
善于自我突破，你就是赢家
孩子在面对一些不太容易完成的事情时，内心总免不了会产生一丝胆怯。作为父母，我们要鼓励孩子勇敢地突破内心的障碍，想办法解决遇到的每一个困难。
瞧，为了参加学校组织的寻宝活动，小熊赫克托尔特意背上了探险者的背包，跃跃欲试。寻宝开始了，赫克托尔突然有些担心自己会不会拖队友的后腿；来到瀑布前，他犹犹豫豫下不了决心靠近瀑布；来到老房子跟前，他又胆怯地不敢上去敲门，结结巴巴地说：“说不定里面有巫婆……” 看到同伴们勇敢地穿过瀑布、敲开老房子的大门，得到了一个又一个寻宝的线索，赫克托尔的心情好低落啊！相信赫克托尔此时的心情很容易引起孩子的共鸣。孩子们会在小熊身上看到自己的影子，并非常想知道接下来发生的事情，想知道赫克托尔后来到底怎么样了。
故事峰回路转，在同伴的鼓励下，赫克托尔终于克服了胆怯心理，找回了自信。他积极地参与到寻找线索的活动中，和同伴们一起努力，成功地完成了任务。合上书的那一刻，孩子一定也跟赫克托尔一样，体会到“自我突破”的力量和快乐。对孩子来说，成长的过程，很多时候就是一个不断突破自我的过程。家长要鼓励孩子进行新的尝试，面对新的挑战

[P6] 得新的能力和体验，从而快乐自信地成长。

孩子总有一天要独立面对这个世界，学会勇敢和坚强。爱孩子，家长就需要不断地为孩子补充“心理营养”。《小熊寻宝记》以孩子们喜欢的动物为主角，通过优美的语言、精致细腻的图画，讲述了一个富有趣味和寓意的故事。和孩子一起读读这个故事，认识小熊赫克托尔吧，让孩子体会“自我突破”的力量与快乐，让孩子认识到：善于自我突破，你就是赢家！

（石家庄市第二幼儿园 谷红岩）

[P7] 今天早上，小熊赫克托尔来到学校时，内心非常激动。因为今天是寻宝的大日子！他特意背上了他的探险者背包——冒险家就应该装备齐全。

[P8] 老师递给他一条红色的领巾，并告诉他：
“赫克托尔，你是红队的一员，和你一起的还有妮娜和马蒂奥。”

[P9] 赫克托尔突然有些担心：我会不会拖大家的后腿呢？
因为妮娜总能在比赛中获胜，而马蒂奥天不怕地不怕。他们才是
真正的冒险家。

[P10] 老师向所有同学解释了比赛的规则，然后宣布：
“第一个线索是：在不干的地方。大家各就各位！预备！出发！”
呼啦啦！所有的孩子都像闪电一样，快速向草地冲去。

[P11] 马蒂奥一边跑一边琢磨：
“不干的地方……那一定是瀑布！我们快去那边看看！”
赫克托尔气喘吁吁地跟在后面。他想跑得再快点儿，不想掉队。
可是，他的背包太重了。

[P13] 他们来到瀑布前面，马蒂奥叹了口气说：
“如果我们靠近瀑布，一定会被淋湿的！

赫克托尔的背包里没有雨伞。
可是，如果他试一试呢？
如果他独自靠近瀑布呢？

[P14] 他想来想去，迟迟下不了决心。
就在他犹犹豫豫的时候，妮娜说：
“好吧！让我来！”

[P15] 妮娜勇敢地爬向瀑布，钻进了水帘里，只听她大叫道：
“哎呀呀！我全身都湿透啦！”
一进到瀑布后面的山洞，她就高兴地大喊：
“我找到线索啦！墙上有幅画，画的是森林里的老房子！”

[P16] “妮娜，干得漂亮！”马蒂奥称赞道。
赫克托尔佩服极了：“冒险家就应该勇往直前……”
从瀑布下来，妮娜冷得直打哆嗦，赫克托尔从背包里掏出一件大毛衣
递给她。

[P17] 他们来到老房子跟前。
这座房子看上去太可怕了，他们全都吓得躲到了围墙后面。
妮娜用颤抖的声音小声问道：“谁敢去敲门啊？”
“我……我不敢去，”赫克托尔结结巴巴地说，“说不定里面有
巫婆……”

[P18] 马蒂奥挽起袖子，坚定地说：
“让我来！我去！”

[P19] 马蒂奥大踏步地走上前去，敲了敲门。
伴着可怕的嘎吱声，大门打开了，里面走出一只老猫头鹰。
马蒂奥用小得不能再小的声音说：
“呃……您……您好，先生，我们正在寻找宝藏的线索……”

[P20] 猫头鹰先生给了马蒂奥一个大大的微笑。
然后，他抓起马蒂奥的手，给了马蒂奥一个苹果：
“这个就是线索。现在，去弄清楚它的含义吧！”

[P22] 妮娜高兴地和马蒂奥拥抱。

赫克托尔想：“冒险家就应该无所畏惧……”
突然，他感到有点儿沮丧。

[P23] “你怎么了，赫克托尔？”马蒂奥和妮娜惊讶地问。
赫克托尔说：“你们都找到线索了。可我呢，就算背了冒险家的背包，也什么都没做成。”

[P24] 妮娜轻轻地说：“冒险家应该帮助他人。你为了不让我着凉，把你的毛衣都借给我了。如果不是你，我身上现在还湿着呢。”

[P25] 赫克托尔找回了信心，他想了想说：
“线索是一个苹果。也许我们需要找到一棵苹果树？”
“我知道，路的尽头有一片田野，那里有一棵苹果树！”马蒂奥喊道。

小伙伴们来到田野，跑到苹果树下。
大家东看看，西看看，在苹果树的周围找，在树干上找，在树枝间找……
但什么线索也没找到。

[P27] 突然，赫克托尔想到一个点子：
“也许我们应该爬到树上去找一找？”

妮娜和马蒂奥有点儿为难……
妮娜不怕被淋湿，马蒂奥不怕巫婆，但他俩谁也不敢爬树。

[P28] 赫克托尔心想：是时候该我鼓起勇气了！
他必须证明自己配得上队友，而且，他本来就会爬树啊！
很快，赫克托尔就爬到了树顶。

[P29] 他没有忘记妮娜的话：“冒险家应该帮助他人。”
于是，他从背包里拿出绳子，牢牢地拴在最高的树枝上。
然后，他冲树下喊：“你们抓紧绳子爬上来，不用怕，没事儿的。”

[P30] 听了赫克托尔的话，妮娜和马蒂奥放心多了，抓着绳子一直爬到了树顶。
“啊！太美啦！”妮娜说，“能爬上来真是太好啦！”

[P31] 妮娜仔细地观察树枝，想看看有没有线索藏在里面。
马蒂奥提议：“赫克托尔，你应该拿出你的望远镜来看一看。”
赫克托尔开始用望远镜观察四周。
突然，他兴奋地大叫道：“在那儿！快看那个小木屋的屋顶！”
“屋顶上有一个十字标记！”马蒂奥喊道。
“宝藏一定藏在那里！”妮娜补充道。

[P33] 他们快速从树上爬下来，飞奔到小木屋那里。
他们打开门。哇哦！他们是第一个到达的！
在屋子的最里面，放着一个木箱子。
小伙伴们赶紧走上前。

[P34] 赫克托尔掀开木箱的盖子。
里面装满了好吃的东西：巧克力饼干、紫罗兰糖浆、草莓水果。
好样的！

[P35] 这时候，老师也来啦。她笑着称赞他们：
“你们是全世界速度最快的冒险家！”
其他队的孩子们推门进来，看到红队的三个小伙伴，
失望地说：“唉！我们输了……”

[P36] 赫克托尔为自己队的团结合作，感到非常自豪。
他提议道：“我们大家一起来吃这些东西吧！”
对啊！冒险家还应该懂得分享！

[P4] Publisher's Note
The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle once said: 'Everyone gets angry; that's not difficult. But to get angry at the right time, in the right place, with the right person, and in the right way—well, that's difficult indeed.' What we now call emotional management is precisely about expressing emotions appropriately, at the right time, in the right place, and toward the right person.
In real life, people are increasingly recognizing the importance of emotional management skills. Those who excel in this area often thrive in various fields; conversely, those who lack this ability, though perhaps intelligent, often struggle in their endeavors.
While emotional management skills may partly stem from innate factors, they ultimately depend on learning and cultivation over time. Early childhood is the golden period for developing emotional management skills. The emotional experiences and habits formed during this period create lasting neural connections in the brain, profoundly influencing a child's physical and mental development.
Currently, reading emotional management picture books together with children is a widely recognized method for cultivating emotional intelligence. High-quality picture books are like seeds of happiness, carried into children's ears by parents' voices, taking root in their hearts, and sprouting with sunlight and rain.
This series of heartwarming animal picture storybooks addresses specific emotional topics for children, illustrating their inner journeys and revealing how they overcome emotional challenges and solve problems. Each book includes a carefully written guide by early childhood education experts, serving as a valuable reference for parents during shared reading.
Let us enjoy a wonderful journey of parent-child reading together with this series.

[P5] Teacher Says to You
Be Good at Breaking Through Yourself, and You Are the Winner
When children face tasks that are not easy to complete, they inevitably feel a bit timid inside. As parents, we should encourage children to bravely break through their inner barriers and find ways to solve every difficulty they encounter.
Look, to participate in a treasure hunt organized by school, little bear Hector specially put on an explorer's backpack, eager to try. The treasure hunt began, and Hector suddenly worried that he might hold his teammates back; when he arrived at the waterfall, he hesitated and couldn't make up his mind to approach it; when he reached the old house, he was timid and dared not knock on the door, stammering, "Maybe there's a witch inside..." Seeing his companions bravely pass through the waterfall and knock on the old house's door, obtaining one clue after another, Hector felt so down! I believe Hector's feelings at this moment can easily resonate with children. Children will see their own reflections in the little bear and will be very curious about what happens next, wondering how Hector eventually turned out.
The story takes a turn. Encouraged by his companions, Hector finally overcame his timidity and regained his confidence. He actively participated in the clue-finding activities, worked hard with his companions, and successfully completed the task. At the moment the book is closed, children will surely feel the power and joy of "self-breakthrough" just like Hector. For children, the process of growth is often a continuous process of breaking through oneself. Parents should encourage children to try new things and face new challenges.

[P6] Gain new abilities and experiences, and grow happily and confidently.

Children will one day have to face the world independently, learning to be brave and strong. Loving children, parents need to continuously provide them with 'psychological nourishment'. 'The Little Bear's Treasure Hunt' features animals beloved by children as protagonists, telling a story full of fun and meaning through beautiful language and delicate illustrations. Read this story together with your child, get to know Little Bear Hector, and let your child experience the power and joy of 'self-breakthrough', helping them realize: being good at self-breakthrough, you are the winner!

(Shijiazhuang No.2 Kindergarten, Gu Hongyan)

[P7] This morning, when little bear Hector arrived at school, he was very excited. Because today was the big day for the treasure hunt! He specially put on his explorer backpack—adventurers should be fully equipped.

School

[P8] The teacher handed him a red scarf and told him:
"Hector, you are a member of the red team, and your teammates are Nina and Matteo."

[P9] Hector suddenly felt a bit worried: What if I hold everyone back?
Because Nina always wins in competitions, and Matteo is fearless. They are the real adventurers.

[P10] The teacher explained the rules of the competition to all the students, then announced:
"The first clue is: in a dry place. Everyone, get ready! On your marks! Get set! Go!"
Whoosh! All the children raced toward the grass like lightning.

[P11] Matteo ran while thinking:
"A dry place... that must be a waterfall! Let's go check it out!"
Hector panted behind. He wanted to run faster, not to fall behind.
But his backpack was too heavy.

[P13] They arrived at the waterfall, and Matéo sighed, saying:
"If we get close to the waterfall, we'll definitely get soaked!"

Hector's backpack didn't have an umbrella.
But what if he tried?
What if he went close to the waterfall alone?

[P14] He thought and thought, but couldn't make up his mind.
Just as he was hesitating, Nina said:
"Alright! Let me try!"

[P15] Nina bravely climbed toward the waterfall, slipped into the water curtain, and shouted: 
"Oh my! I'm completely soaked!"
As soon as she entered the cave behind the waterfall, she happily shouted: 
"I found the clue! There's a painting on the wall, showing an old house in the forest!"

[P16] "Nina, you did a great job!" Matteo praised.
Hector was deeply impressed: "Adventurers should always move forward..."
After coming down from the waterfall, Nina was shivering from the cold. Hector took out a big sweater from his backpack and handed it to her.

[P17] They arrived at the old house.
This house looked too scary, and they all hid behind the wall.
Nina asked in a trembling voice, "Who dares to knock on the door?"
"I... I don't dare to go," Hector stammered, "Maybe there's a witch inside..."

[P18] Matio rolled up his sleeves and said firmly:
"Let me do it! I'll go!"

[P19] Matteo took a big step forward and knocked on the door.
With a terrible creaking sound, the door opened, and an old owl came out.
Matteo said in a voice so small it could hardly be heard:
"Uh... you... hello, sir, we are looking for clues to the treasure..."

[P20] Mr. Owl gave Matéo a big smile.
Then, he took Matéo's hand and gave him an apple:
"This is the clue. Now, go figure out its meaning!"

[P22] Nina happily hugged Matteo.

Hector thought, "An adventurer should be fearless..."
Suddenly, he felt a bit sad.

[P23] "What's wrong, Hector?" Martio and Nina asked in surprise.
Hector said, "You both found clues. But me? Even with the adventurer's backpack, I didn't accomplish anything."

[P24] Nina said softly, "An adventurer should help others. You lent me your sweater to keep me warm. If it weren't for you, I'd still be wet right now."

[P25] Hector regained his confidence. He thought for a moment and said:
"The clue is an apple. Maybe we need to find an apple tree?"
"I know, at the end of the path there's a field with an apple tree!" Matéo shouted.

The friends arrived at the field and ran to the apple tree.
They looked here and there, searching around the tree, on the trunk, between the branches...
But they found no clue.

[P27] Suddenly, Hector had an idea:
"Maybe we should climb up the tree and look around?"

Nina and Matteo were a bit hesitant...
Nina wasn't afraid of getting wet, and Matteo wasn't afraid of witches, but neither of them dared to climb a tree.

[P28] Hector thought: It's time for me to gather my courage!
He had to prove he was worthy of his teammates, and besides, he could climb trees!
Soon, Hector climbed to the top of the tree.

25

[P29] He didn't forget Nina's words: 'Adventurers should help others.'
So, he took the rope from his backpack and securely tied it to the highest branch.
Then, he called down to the tree: 'Grab the rope and climb up, don't be afraid, it's okay.'

[P30] After hearing Hector's words, Nina and Mateo felt much more at ease, and they climbed up the rope all the way to the top of the tree.
"Ah! So beautiful!" Nina said, "It's so great to be able to climb up here!"

[P31] Nina carefully examined the branches, looking for any clues hidden inside.
Matteo suggested, "Hector, you should take out your telescope and have a look."
Hector began to observe his surroundings through the telescope.
Suddenly, he excitedly shouted, "There! Look at the roof of that little wooden house!"
"There's a cross mark on the roof!" Matteo shouted.
"The treasure must be hidden there!" Nina added.

[P33] They quickly climbed down from the tree and ran to the little wooden house.
They opened the door. Wow! They were the first to arrive!
Inside, at the very back of the house, there was a wooden box.
The friends hurried forward.

[P34] Hector lifts the lid of the wooden chest.
Inside are delicious treats: chocolate cookies, violet syrup, and strawberry fruit.
Well done!

[P35] At this moment, the teacher arrived too. She smiled and praised them:
"You are the fastest adventurers in the world!"
The children from other teams pushed the door open, saw the three companions from the red team,
and said disappointedly: "Ah! We lost..."

[P1] 本页为绘本《小熊寻宝记》的封面，展示了小熊和一群森林动物朋友在森林中快乐奔跑的场景，书名、作者、出版社等信息清晰可见。
[P2] 本页为绘本《小熊寻宝记》的扉页，展示了书名、作者、译者、出版社等信息，以及主角小熊背着书包站在草地上的插图。
[P3] 本页为绘本《小熊寻宝记》的版权页，列出了图书的出版信息、作者、译者、出版社、ISBN、CIP数据、版权信息、编辑团队、出版发行信息、印刷信息及定价等。
[P4] 本页为《小熊寻宝记》的出版者的话，阐述了情绪管理的重要性，强调幼儿时期是培养情绪管理能力的黄金期，并介绍了该系列图画书通过亲子共读帮助孩子认识和管理情绪的教育理念。
[P5] 本页为绘本《小熊寻宝记》的导读页，以‘老师对你说’为标题，通过讲述小熊赫克托尔在寻宝活动中从胆怯到克服困难、实现自我突破的故事，引导家长鼓励孩子勇敢面对挑战，培养其自信心和解决问题的能力。
[P6] 本页为《小熊寻宝记》的导读页，引用石家庄市第二幼儿园谷红岩老师的话，强调通过共读绘本帮助孩子补充‘心理营养’，培养勇敢坚强的品质，体会自我突破的快乐，并配有一幅小熊为同伴递上毛衣的插图。
[P7] 小熊赫克托尔早上来到学校，为即将开始的寻宝活动感到非常激动，并背上了他的探险者背包。画面中还有其他小动物同学在校园里活动。
[P8] 老师为小熊赫克托尔分发红色领巾，并告知他成为红队成员，队友是妮娜和马蒂奥。
[P9] 小熊赫克托尔在寻宝活动开始前，因担心自己拖累队友而感到不安，认为队友妮娜和马蒂奥才是真正的冒险家。
[P10] 老师宣布寻宝活动的第一个线索后，所有孩子兴奋地冲向草地开始寻找。
[P11] 在寻宝活动中，马蒂奥兴奋地推测线索指向瀑布并带头奔跑，而赫克托尔因背包太重而气喘吁吁地跟在后面，担心自己掉队。
[P12] 画面中，三只小动物在林间小路上奔跑，其中一只狼形角色兴奋地指向前方，一只小熊在后方跟随，另一只松鼠形角色在前景处喘息，似乎体力不支。背景是绿树和草地，右下角有二维码及宣传文字。
[P13] 小熊赫克托尔和队友马蒂奥来到瀑布前，马蒂奥担心会被淋湿，而赫克托尔的背包里没有雨伞，内心开始思考是否要独自尝试靠近瀑布。
[P14] 小熊赫克托尔在瀑布前犹豫不决，担心自己无法靠近，这时队友妮娜主动提出由她来尝试。
[P15] 妮娜勇敢地钻进瀑布水帘，进入后面的山洞，并在墙上发现了一幅画着森林老房子的线索。
[P16] 妮娜成功穿过瀑布水帘找到线索后，马蒂奥称赞她，赫克托尔深受感动并从背包中拿出毛衣为她御寒。
[P17] 三只小动物来到一座看起来很可怕的老房子前，因害怕而躲在围墙后，妮娜询问谁敢去敲门，赫克托尔表示不敢，担心里面有巫婆。
[P18] 在老房子前，马蒂奥主动请缨，表示要上前敲门，而赫克托尔和妮娜则在一旁露出惊讶和担忧的表情。
[P19] 马蒂奥鼓起勇气上前敲开老房子的门，门后走出一只老猫头鹰，他紧张地向对方询问宝藏线索。
[P20] 猫头鹰先生给了马蒂奥一个苹果作为线索，并鼓励他去弄清楚其含义。
[P22] 妮娜和马蒂奥拥抱庆祝，而赫克托尔因觉得自己不够勇敢而感到沮丧。
[P23] 赫克托尔因自己未能找到线索而感到沮丧，队友马蒂奥和妮娜关切地询问他，他坦言自己虽然背着冒险家的背包却一事无成。
[P24] 妮娜安慰因未能找到线索而沮丧的赫克托尔，感谢他借毛衣给自己御寒，强调冒险家应互相帮助。
[P25] 赫克托尔和马蒂奥根据苹果线索前往田野寻找苹果树，但仔细搜寻后一无所获。
[P26] 三只小动物站在一棵结满红苹果的树下，赫克托尔躲在树后显得沮丧，马蒂奥和妮娜站在一旁，妮娜张开双臂似乎在鼓励或解释什么，画面右下角有二维码和宣传文字。
[P27] 赫克托尔提议爬树寻找线索，但妮娜和马蒂奥因害怕爬树而感到为难。
[P28] 赫克托尔鼓起勇气，决定爬树寻找线索，并很快爬到了树顶。
[P29] 赫克托尔爬到树顶后，想起妮娜的话，决定帮助队友，于是拿出绳子拴在树枝上，并鼓励他们顺着绳子爬上来。
[P30] 妮娜和马蒂奥在赫克托尔的帮助下，抓着绳子爬上了苹果树顶，妮娜感叹景色美丽并为成功爬上来感到高兴。
[P31] 赫克托尔用望远镜观察四周，发现小木屋屋顶有十字标记，妮娜和马蒂奥确认这是宝藏的线索。
[P32] 三只小动物在苹果树上，赫克托尔用望远镜观察远处山坡上的小木屋，屋顶有红色十字标记，妮娜和马蒂奥在树上指向目标，确认这是宝藏线索。
[P33] 三只小动物从苹果树上下来，飞奔到小木屋，发现门开着，他们是第一个到达的，并看到屋内最里面有一个木箱子，于是赶紧上前查看。
[P34] 三只小动物打开小木屋里的木箱，发现里面装满了巧克力饼干、紫罗兰糖浆和草莓水果等好吃的东西，箱子上贴着写有“好样的！”的纸条。
[P35] 老师称赞红队的三个小伙伴是全世界速度最快的冒险家，其他队的孩子们推门进来后发现他们已先到达，感到失望。
[P36] 赫克托尔为团队的团结合作感到自豪，提议大家一起分享宝藏里的食物，其他小动物纷纷表示赞同，认为冒险家应该懂得分享。
[P37] 三只小动物（狼、熊、狐狸）站在石墙旁，面向右侧的小木屋，似乎在讨论或准备进入。画面右下角有二维码和推广文字，但无对话或叙述性文字。
